The independent reviewer (OpenAI, gpt-6-luna, deep tier) found no correctness bugs in `src/router/escalation.ts`, so there is no top finding from it. It read the file, its caller, the policy code, the tests and conductor.md §4. It did not run tests, type-check or lint, and rated its confidence medium.

I agree. I read the file myself and found nothing that breaks the ladder. The retry, fallback, tier-up and max-attempts branches match the spec.

The closest thing to a concern is `src/router/escalation.ts:66`. Tier-up uses `alive[0]`, the most-preferred live provider, rather than `last.provider`. After a fallback, the tier-up can therefore go back to the first provider, not the one that just failed. That fits "preference order", so it is a design choice and not a bug. I'd leave it, but it should be a deliberate choice.
